sources.entry: EventSchedule - Share events, sell tickets, and bring communities together. (Source Code) AAL PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: Event Schedule is an open-source, self-hostable PHP/Laravel platform for publishing event calendars, selling tickets, taking registrations and running community event pages.
summary.what_it_does: It lets a venue, performer or community publish schedules and events, including recurring events with per-date exceptions, public, draft, internal and unlisted visibility, and public event request queues. Ticketing covers paid tickets through Stripe, PayPal, Payfast, Razorpay, Invoice Ninja, payment links or cash, plus promo codes, waitlists, QR tickets, a door scanner and a drag-and-drop seating plan builder. It also provides appointment booking, two-way sync with Google Calendar, Outlook and CalDAV, and .ics/webcal import. Optional AI features (Gemini or OpenAI keys) can create events from text or flyers, and newsletters, subscribers, analytics, a REST API and HMAC-signed webhooks are included. Optional integrations activate only after the matching credentials are added to .env, and a fresh install makes only a daily GitHub update check and a monthly DB-IP GeoIP download.
use_cases: sell tickets for a venue or show
take free RSVPs with capacity limits
sync events with Google or Outlook calendars
run a newsletter to event followers
check in ticket holders at the door with QR codes
how_to_run: git clone the repository, then cd into the dockerfiles directory
Manual: create an empty MySQL database, extract eventschedule.zip, point the web root at public
Run cp .env.example .env, leave APP_URL blank, open the site and follow the setup wizard
Add the cron entry: * * * * * php /path/to/eventschedule/artisan schedule:run
notable: All paid-plan features of the hosted version are included in selfhosted installs, with no license keys or platform fees on ticket sales
No telemetry; JS, CSS and fonts are vendored instead of loaded from a CDN
Browser setup wizard tests the database, runs migrations and writes config; updates are one click from the admin panel
Supports 12 interface languages including right-to-left Hebrew and Arabic
Curator schedule type automatically pulls in events from the venues and performers it lists
caveats: Requires PHP 8.2+, MySQL 5.7+ or MariaDB 10.3+, a web server, HTTPS and a cron entry
Guest pages on a selfhosted install keep a small Event Schedule credit linking to the project
Selfhosted installs are single-user by default; registration must be enabled with ALLOW_REGISTRATION=true
